title: Event realignment sandbox and safe-playback tooling for analytics backfills
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Provide a safe, sandboxed environment and a lightweight playback toolset to run idempotent, partial backfills and event realignment jobs against the telemetry/usage analytics pipelines. This work aims to enable engineers and SREs to validate backfill logic, surface schema drift, and compare pre/post metrics without impacting production metrics stores or downstream customers. Deliverables: sandbox cluster config, dry-run validator, checksum-based gating, microshard playback orchestrator, and a stats diff dashboard for quick validation.
implementation_steps: Create isolated sandbox namespace in analytics cluster with synthetic traffic and snapshot restore of latest telemetry partition metadata
Design and implement dry-run validator that simulates transformations and emits sample outputs + checksum signatures
Build microshard playback orchestrator that can run partial windows with resume tokens and rate limits
Add preflight gating based on schema/field-level checksums and sample-value ranges
Wire lightweight diff pipeline to compute delta metrics (counts, cardinalities, pct-change) and surface in a temporary dashboard
Integrate GitHub-based PR workflow: PR triggers sandbox run and posts results summary to PR and Confluence
Document runbooks, failure modes, and rollback guidance; add RBAC to prevent accidental production playback
risks: Accidental production writes if RBAC or config isolation fails
Large backfills could saturate cluster I/O if rate limits are insufficient
Schema drift may cause silent data loss if not detected early
False positives/negatives in checksum gating leading to aborted runs or unsafe playbacks
testing_plan: Unit tests for dry-run validator and checksum computation
End-to-end sandbox runs against synthetic datasets with injected schema drift
Chaos test: simulate partial failures and ensure resume tokens permit safe continuation
Load test: run microshard playback at target throughput to validate throttling
Pre-merge CI job: run lightweight sandbox against representative sample and attach results to PR
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox namespace can be provisioned from a single CLI command
Dry-run validator reports deterministic checksums and sample diffs for a given input
Playback orchestrator supports start/stop/resume for microshard windows and enforces rate limits
Automated preflight gates prevent playback if checksum or schema checks fail
Dashboard displays delta metrics and flags >5% cardinality or count divergence
Runbook reviewed and signed off by SRE and Data Platform leads
updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed comparing checksum strategies (CRC32 vs MurmurHash). Team chose MurmurHash for field-order tolerance.
2025-02-18: Prototype dry-run validator implemented; emits sample rows and checksum signatures. PR opened: telemetry-tools#482.
2025-02-24: Sandbox provisioning script added to infra repo; found RBAC edge-case where service account needed extra permissions.
2025-03-01: First end-to-end sandbox run completed against synthetic dataset. Observed a 7% cardinality shift due to a previously-unmapped user_agent variant; added mapping rule.
2025-03-05: Rate-limiter added to orchestrator to protect cluster; initial manual review by Data Platform and SRE teams scheduled for 2025-03-07
notes: Trade-offs: We prioritize an explicit dry-run + gating approach rather than optimistic patching. That increases developer friction on small fixes but greatly reduces accidental regressions for high-impact datasets.
Longer-term: Consider integrating with Optimize to recommend safe shard sizes and quantile-based throttle defaults.
Operational: Keep sandbox snapshot TTL to 72h and enforce automatic cleanup to limit costs.
